name: end
summary: Reloads main entry 0, clears the active-lane mask and marks the script halted: main index +2576 = 0, stage +2580 = 0, cursor +2652 = root[0][0], lane word +3288 = 0, state +2659 = 2.
control_flow: returns the reloaded cursor; the interpreter continues from there

name: contents_return
summary: Resumes the saved contents cursor and switches the selection stage back to 0 (contents). Logged as "CONTENTS TBL END".

name: sub_contents_return
summary: Resumes the saved sub-contents cursor and switches the selection stage to 1 (sub contents). Logged as "SUB CONTENTS TBL END".

name: ground_area_move
summary: Runs the current-area ground-move state machine through the table at actor +2900 -> +24, keyed by current area +2040. Clamps the movement record and step indices +2657/+2658, checks progress/distance, may select another motion script through 0x108604e0 and update current/saved kind-9 fields, and finally restores and clears saved cursor +2648 and clears +2581/+3231. Selectors 4 and 5 share an entry, but are not fully equivalent: only selector 4 passes the explicit selector == 4 guard for final area/position/heading placement when saved kind is 9 and the native placement conditions hold. This is not a plain subscript return.
writes: state affected by called movement/area helpers
control_flow: replaces cursor with a movement script or saved +2648; may change world position, area and movement state

name: ground_area_move_snap
summary: Ground-area move completion/placement state-machine variant. In normal command mode, saved kind 9 and selector 6 enter the placement path directly, subject to a valid destination-area record and actor +3187. It copies the record position and previous-position snapshot, heading and mapped area, refreshes area state, then restores and clears saved cursor +2648 and clears +2581/+3231. In command mode it may instead select the step motion script or reload the main cursor. It is not equivalent to selectors 4/5 or a generic return.
writes: state affected by called movement/area helpers
control_flow: replaces cursor with a movement script, main entry or saved +2648; may place actor and change area

name: unko_end
summary: Hard reset to the first main entry: main index +2576 = 0, stage +2580 = 0, cursor +2652 = root[0][0], lane word +3288 = 0, state +2659 = 2. Logged as "UNKO_END".

name: no_floor_end
summary: Reset identical to 0xff/0x00, reached when the route has no floor. Logged as "NO_FLOOR_END".

name: find_ng_end
summary: Resets the main selection and command-lane mask, then clears the selected player tracking bit +2687, retention timer +2688, awareness score +2788 and hate score +2824 using +2612 & 0x0f. If +2612 is 0xff, no player bookkeeping is cleared. It does not clear +2612 itself or the detection mask +2684. Native log names this FIND_NG_END and NOT_FOUND_PL.
control_flow: returns the reloaded cursor; the NOT_FOUND path returns through the default branch

name: clear_lane8
summary: Clears lane bit 0x0008. If lane bit 0x0001 is still set it resumes root[2][+2595]; otherwise it resets the main index/stage/cursor to root[0][0] and marks script state +2659 as 2; other command-lane bits are not cleared here.
control_flow: branch on the remaining lane mask

name: clear_lane4
summary: Clears lane bit 0x0004. If lane bit 0x0001 is still set it resumes root[2][+2595]; otherwise it resets the main index/stage/cursor to root[0][0] and marks script state +2659 as 2; other command-lane bits are not cleared here.
control_flow: branch on the remaining lane mask

name: clear_lane2
summary: Reloads the current main selection, clears command-lane bit 0x0002 and calls 0x1084fb80(em, 0). If route bit 0x0001 remains, resumes root[2][+2595]; otherwise resets main index/stage/cursor to root[0][0] and sets script state +2659 to 2. This preserves the native perception-profile helper side effects.
control_flow: branch on the remaining lane mask

name: area_end
summary: Returns the saved area-handler continuation +2616 and clears wait byte +2621. Compares signed area-list count +2844 with selected index +2845: when count > index it returns directly; otherwise +2620==0 invalidates both fields to 0xFF, while nonzero +2620 resets the selected index to zero. Native log: AREA_END.
control_flow: returns +2616; may end the movement state

name: find_end
summary: Completes the player-detected/find command. When command-mode byte +2739 is zero, calls Em_Mode_Chg(em, 1) at 0x108693e0 and then copies mode +2680 into snapshot +2600, not +2681. In all cases reloads root[0][0], clears command-lane word +3288 and sets script state +2659 to 2. Native log: FIND_END Em_Mode_Chg(em, EM_MODE_ATTACK).

name: kehai_end
summary: Ends the alert (kehai) route: clears lane bit 0x0010. If lane bit 0x0001 is still set it resumes root[2][+2595] ("route_ptr_set( em, em->cmd_route_act )"); otherwise it reloads the main entry and marks the network command state ("em_cmd_top( em ) ... EM_NET_CMD").
control_flow: branch on the remaining lane mask

name: route_move_end
summary: Completes one route-move step. Refreshes the reference position, measures horizontal distance and compares against the larger of the species radius and the actor-size-derived bound. If still far, resumes root[2][+2595]. On arrival increments progress +2842, clears +3250, then selects waypoint +2840 by mode +2592: 0 chooses from [0,+2843) excluding the current waypoint using +1096 (or falls back to zero if no candidate); 1 reads root[2][+2593][progress]; 2 increments the waypoint. It then resumes root[2][+2595]. It does not perform the route-loop completion test handled by FF FF.
control_flow: resumes root[2][+2595] through 0x108604c0; requires initialized route mode/counters/tables

name: loop_count
summary: Tests unsigned byte route progress +2842 against unsigned byte limit +2841. Below the limit, resumes root[2][+2594]. Otherwise clears command-lane bit 0x0001 and asks 0x10860700 to select the next cursor. It does not increment progress itself; FF FE does that on arrival. Requires the native route continuation context rather than a lexical loop stack.

name: re-dispatch
summary: Any selector outside 0x00..0x06 and 0xf5..0xff is not a control subcommand. The handler returns the selector pointer unchanged and writes it to +2652, so the interpreter dispatches that byte as an ordinary top-level opcode; only the 0xff prefix has been consumed. Top-level 0xf5..0xfe bytes without this prefix instead hit the interpreter default stop path.
control_flow: returns the pointer to the selector byte
